newsitem.title: UK: AMB - UK's Labour plans no curb on tobacco sponsor.
newsitem.headline: AMB - UK's Labour plans no curb on tobacco sponsor.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party has no plans to restrict corporate sponsorship by tobacco companies of sports events if it wins the next election, a Labour MP said on Thursday.
"Labour has no plans for the restriction of tobacco sponsorship in sport...," Kate Hoey, Labour's Member of Parliament for Vauxhall, told a business conference in London.
Hoey said any future Labour government would, however, stick to the party's previously-stated position to ban tobacco advertising in Britain.

Hoey was addressing an annual conference of the Incorporated Society of British Advertisers Ltd (ISBA), whose 300 corporate members spend an estimated 2.5 billion pounds ($3.9 billion) on advertising, sponsorship and other communications areas.

British advertising agencies and brand-name companies that spend money on advertising have said they were worried a possible future Labour government would be more antagonistic to the advertising industry than the ruling Conservative Party.
But Hoey appeared to want to calm industry fears, saying sponsorship by tobacco companies provided an important contribution to sports events.
"My own feelings are that the present sponsorship by the tobacco industry should continue and that it will be the EU (European Union) that will be making the strategic moves," she said.

"With multi-national TV it is difficult to see how much change could be made to the regulations on tobacco-sponsored sport. Many tobacco sponsors do provide a significant amount to sport in a year (approximately 9.0 million pounds ($14.0 million)," Hoey said.
Bob Wootton, ISBA's director of media services, welcomed Hoey's comments, saying the Labour MP took a friendlier approach to tobacco sponsorship than he had expected.
"I'd expected a slightly harder stance, so I was quite reassured," he told Reuters.

In the United States, President Bill Clinton announced new regulations in August to reduce the appeal and access of tobacco products to young people, including limiting tobacco sponsorship of sporting or entertainment events.
